chunks: And in the narration of Al-Husayn ibn Alwan from Amr ibn Khalid from Zayd ibn Ali from his forefathers (peace be upon them) from Ali (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) mentioned jihad, and a woman said to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family): 'O Messenger of Allah, do women have any share in this?' He replied: 'Yes, for a woman, from the time of her pregnancy until she gives birth and until she weans her child, she receives a reward equal to that of a person stationed in the way of Allah. And if she dies during that period, she will have the same status as a martyr.'

key_terms.الْجِهَادُ: Striving or exertion, specifically in the path of God
key_terms.الْمُرَابِطُ: A person stationed at the frontier or in continuous readiness for battle

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for women in jihad according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih highlights the concept of 'Jihad al-Batin' (inner jihad) for women, framing the physical and spiritual endurance of pregnancy, childbirth, and nursing as a continuous state of devotion equivalent to the warrior's vigilance (Murabita). Shia scholars emphasize that this elevates domestic duties to the level of major acts of worship, ensuring that women are not excluded from the high merit of martyrdom if they pass away during these periods, thereby balancing the gendered expressions of jihad in Islamic jurisprudence.
